Ensure that this behavior is consistent with the intended design and does not introduce unexpected side effects, especially in cases where the context might not be a `CoordinatorRewriteContext`.
Adding `DataTierFieldMapper.PARSER` to the built-in metadata mappers is correct. Ensure that this mapper does not conflict with existing mappers and that its presence does not introduce any issues.

The addition of `DataTierFieldMapper` to various test cases ensures that the new field type is properly tested. Verify that these tests cover all necessary scenarios and edge cases for the new field type.

The change in `createCoordinatorContext` to include an empty string for the tier parameter is correct if this is the intended default behavior. Ensure that this default value does not cause issues in any part of the application where a coordinator context is used.

review_comment:
We are potentially artificially limiting the coordinator tier rewrite to [only indices that have the time range configured](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/114990/files#diff-0ad1800461d83a801b07a1207f4395615a0e9b6b5aad9ded33bda88e0f784d47R56) (partially mounted indices). We don't have to have this limitation for the `_tier` coordination rewrite however, the current implementation is sufficient for skipping frozen (where all indices do indeed have the `@timestamp` and `event.ingested` ranges). 

In the interest of keeping this fix targeted and contained I believe it's a good compromise for now but curious what you think.
now that this is merged, do we want to do the follow-up to allow filtering on tier to work on all indices?
